commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor sources to module coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
The classes sit in the default package, use `/* */` where Javadoc
belongs, and break the naming, import order and indentation rules. The
banner rows in Serangooner run past the 120 character hard limit, and
`delete` repeats the task number parsing that `updateStatus` already
does.

Let's move every class into a `serangooner` package, replace the old
headers with Javadoc, and bring the layout in line with the standard.
The repeated parsing moves into a single `parseTaskNumber` helper, so
the argument rules for `mark`, `unmark` and `delete` live in one place.

Program output is unchanged. Both the full command set and the argument
error paths were diffed against a build of the previous sources.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: CLAUDE.md: Replace pointer with full rules
commitResults.messageBody:
CLAUDE.md forwards to AGENTS.md, which frames the repository as a
generic starter template and gives the module conventions as bare links.
The commit format, the Java coding standard and the tagging workflow
have to be looked up mid-task, so they get missed.

Let's spell the rules out in CLAUDE.md: project facts, the commit
message convention, the se-education Java standard, the JUnit layout,
the tag-and-push steps, and the AI citation policy. AGENTS.md stays put
as the course's own file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add /done command for milestone release
commitResults.messageBody:
Closing an increment means compiling, reviewing the diff against the
standard, committing, tagging with the exact increment ID, then pushing
the commit and the tag as separate steps. Done by hand this invites a
missed step, and the standing rule against committing unasked has to be
waived each time.

Let's capture the sequence as a slash command taking the tag name as its
argument, mirroring the Codex skill in `.codex/skills/done`. Invoking it
counts as authorisation to commit and push, for that one milestone only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-7: Save and load tasks from the hard disk
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks entered in one session are lost the moment Serangooner exits, so
the list must be rebuilt by hand on every run.

Let's persist the list to ./data/serangooner.txt, reading it when the
list is constructed and writing it back after every edit. TaskList owns
the Storage instance so the file cannot fall out of step with what the
user sees, and each task class encodes its own line so that adding a
task type later needs only one more override.

A line that cannot be understood is skipped and reported in a short
startup message rather than aborting the load, so one damaged line
never costs the user the rest of the list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Let each task type read its own saved line
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage both dispatches on the type code and works out where each
field sits, so the layout of a saved line is settled in two places
at once: the task class writes it, and Storage independently reads
it back. Storage also signals a bad line by throwing, which load()
catches purely to count it, even though a damaged line is expected
input rather than a fault.

Let's give each task type a fromSaveFields factory beside its
toSaveFormat, returning an empty optional when the line cannot be
read. Reading and writing then sit together in the class that owns
the format, Storage shrinks to a switch on the type code, and the
load path no longer uses exceptions for ordinary control flow.

A shared readSaveLine helper on Task holds the checks every type
makes, so a saved line is accepted only with the exact field count
expected. A description containing the field separator is therefore
reported as unreadable instead of being loaded back mangled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-8: Store dates and times as date objects
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadlines and events hold their dates as raw text, so the bot cannot
tell a date from any other string handed to it. Nothing can be
compared or filtered, and whatever the user types is echoed straight
back.

Let's parse both into a TaskDateTime, which wraps a LocalDateTime and
remembers whether a time of day was given. Dates are read as
2019-10-15 or 2019-10-15 1800 and shown as 15 Oct 2019 or
20 Oct 2019, 6:00PM, while the save file keeps the input format so a
saved task reads back as the value that was written.

One class owns every formatter, so the two task types share a parser
instead of each growing its own. A date that no longer parses skips
its line on load, joining the unreadable lines the loader already
reports, so one stale date never costs the user the rest of the list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to view tasks on or between dates
commitResults.messageBody:
Dates are held as real dates, but the only way to find what falls on a
given day is to read the whole list by eye. A list that grows past a
screenful makes that impractical.

Let's add "on <date> [to <date>]", which lists the deadlines and
events falling on a single date or touching any date in a range.
Matching goes through Task.isWithin, so each task type decides for
itself what falling within a range means and the command never has to
test what type a task is.

Both listings share one renderer, and it numbers tasks by their
position in the full list, so a number read off a filtered view stays
usable with mark, unmark and delete.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject events that end before they start
commitResults.messageBody:
An event takes any two dates, so one running from 16 Oct to 14 Oct is
stored as written. That event can never be found again: matching looks
for a span running forwards, and a backwards span covers no day at
all, so it answers no date query.

Let's reject the pair when the end falls before the start, comparing
through TaskDateTime so a time of day counts as much as the date. A
saved event whose dates disagree is skipped on load, like any other
line the loader cannot make sense of.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
